messages.content: Back from the Oregon loop and I already have the next puzzle. Can you help me shape an early October North Texas route before I send it for approval? Draft is Sun Oct 6 to Thu Oct 10: Monday morning counselor breakfast in Plano, Monday evening fair in Dallas, Tuesday high-school visits in Fort Worth, Wednesday 2-5 transfer fair in Waco, and Thursday late-morning community college meeting near Round Rock. I need to compare open-jaw flying, Dallas round-trip flying, and just driving from Salt Lake with materials.

Yes. A few details affect whether the routing is truly workable: how many materials are you moving, what hotel or airfare caps should I keep in mind, and do you have Sunday or Thursday flight-time limits?

Probably five boxes plus the banner tube if I don't ship. Hotel cap is $185 before tax unless there's a reason. Airfare can be higher if it saves real staff time. I can leave Sunday afternoon but not morning. Thursday meeting should be done around noon; I'd rather not get back to Salt Lake near midnight. One easy connection is fine.

Initial read: open-jaw is the plan to defend. Option 1, SLC to Dallas and Austin back to SLC, follows the route south and avoids a Thursday backtrack; the trade-offs are possible higher airfare, a one-way rental fee, and a materials plan. Option 2, Dallas round trip, may price cleaner and avoids a car drop fee, but Round Rock back to DFW is about 3 to 3.5 hours before traffic, so any late meeting or I-35 slowdown makes the return less reliable. Option 3, driving from Salt Lake, solves materials but costs multiple travel days and fatigue; I would only use it if flying plus shipping becomes impossible.
Can you sketch the overnight areas? I can handle three hotels if it actually helps, but I don't want to make a mess.

I would use three hotel areas. Sunday and Monday: Plano, Richardson, or Addison, not downtown Dallas. That protects the Plano breakfast and gives better odds of free parking and breakfast under the cap. Tuesday: either Fort Worth south/Arlington if the visits run late, or Waco if you can leave Fort Worth by mid-afternoon. Wednesday: Round Rock or Georgetown after the Waco fair if the fair really ends around 5. That puts you close to Thursday's meeting and Austin airport.
The Dallas fair load-in starts 4:30 and ends at 8:30. I am a little worried about downtown parking with boxes.

Then I would not pick an over-cap downtown hotel just to be near the fair. Stay north where parking and breakfast are simpler, then pre-reserve a garage or official event lot for Monday from about 3:30 to 9:15. Leave Plano/Richardson by 3:15. Also choose an SUV or at least a vehicle with covered cargo space so the boxes are not visible while you are at dinner or between visits.
What if I fly into Love Field instead? Does that reduce the Monday pain?

Love Field can work if the fare and arrival time are good, but it does not change the route enough to chase it. It is a little easier for central Dallas, while DFW usually has stronger SLC nonstop options and is fine for Plano/Richardson. I would compare both Dallas airports, but I would not give up a good DFW Sunday afternoon nonstop for a weaker Love Field connection.
For materials, I don't know if I should check, ship, or drive.

I would not drive from Salt Lake just for five boxes. Best plan: ship the heavy brochures to the first confirmed receiving point, ideally the Monday fair or the first hotel if they will accept packages without a big handling fee. Carry the scanner, tablecloth, small counselor packets, and anything irreplaceable. If you must fly with the banner tube, treat it like a checked item and keep the receipt. After Dallas, keep remaining materials in the SUV for Waco and Round Rock.
How bad is the Dallas round trip if we need cheaper airfare?

It is not impossible, but it is the weaker operational plan. After a late-morning Round Rock meeting, you would drive north to DFW, refuel, return the car, and clear security before an evening flight. That is a long final day and leaves little buffer if the meeting runs over or I-35 is slow. I would only switch to Dallas round trip if Austin return pricing is dramatically worse or if the Austin options require multiple stops, long layovers, or a very late Salt Lake arrival.
Breakfast and dinner access matter because the days are going to be weird. Flag that in the approval note.

For hotel areas, I would write it this way: North Dallas/Plano-Richardson for Sunday and Monday because it supports the Plano breakfast, has free-parking hotels under cap, and still works for the Dallas fair with pre-reserved event parking. Waco Tuesday if you can reach it after Fort Worth, because it reduces the Wednesday transfer-fair scramble. Round Rock/Georgetown Wednesday because it protects Thursday morning and has easier dinner options than arriving late from Waco on Thursday morning.
Can you give me the approval note version, not too fancy?

Approval recommendation: approve open-jaw air into Dallas and out of Austin, plus a one-way SUV rental. The trip moves south from Plano/Dallas to Fort Worth, Waco, and Round Rock, so returning from Austin avoids a 3-plus-hour Thursday backtrack to DFW after the final meeting. Hotel plan is two nights in Plano/Richardson, one night in Waco, and one night in Round Rock/Georgetown, prioritizing included breakfast and free or simple parking under the $185 pre-tax cap. Dallas fair parking should be pre-reserved separately because downtown hotels near the fair are likely to be over cap or have paid parking.
Last thing: if Austin return options are terrible, what would you check before switching back to Dallas?

I would first check Austin departures after about 2:30 pm on Thursday, on one ticket, with no more than one comfortable connection and a Salt Lake arrival before roughly 9:30. A late nonstop is a backup if the price is reasonable, but it creates a long airport wait or a late night. I would switch back to Dallas only if Austin is several hundred dollars higher after the one-way car fee, or if the only Austin options are unreliable connections. For refundable room holds once dates are firm, start with Plano/Richardson for Sunday/Monday, Waco for Tuesday, and Round Rock/Georgetown for Wednesday.

messages.content: Update on Texas before anything is booked: Fort Worth visits moved earlier Tuesday, the Waco transfer fair moved to Tuesday evening, and Round Rock stayed Thursday late morning. The Dallas fair venue also warned that nearby parking can fill before load-in. The closest hotels I found are either over the nightly cap or don't include breakfast. Can you rerank the plans?

The change makes the open-jaw plan even stronger. My ranking now: 1, fly into Dallas and home from Austin; 2, Dallas round trip only if Austin pricing or flight quality falls apart; 3, driving from Salt Lake, still not worth the time. Overnight sequence: Sunday/Monday in Plano or Richardson, Tuesday in Waco after the evening fair, Wednesday in Round Rock or north Austin.
For the Austin return, I see a late nonstop that lands around 10 and an afternoon one-stop that gets home around 7:30 with a 75- to 90-minute connection. Which one should I ask them to approve?

Ask for the afternoon one-stop if it is on one ticket and the connection is truly in that 75- to 90-minute range. It gets you home at a better hour and avoids sitting around Austin all evening after the Round Rock meeting. The late nonstop is a good backup, but the one-stop is the more humane workday.
Should I try Tuesday night north Austin anyway so Thursday is easy? I hate hotel changes, but I also don't want a late drive.

I would not drive Waco to north Austin after an evening fair with boxes. That is the exact kind of late, tired drive that causes meal and check-in problems. Stay in Waco Tuesday, then use Wednesday to reposition to Round Rock. You still end up near the Thursday meeting without making Tuesday night miserable.
The fair is near Market Center. The close hotels are about $215, or cheaper but with paid breakfast and $25 to $30 parking.

Then use a Plano/Richardson hotel for Sunday and Monday and solve the fair with a reserved garage. The close hotel does not actually remove the parking issue because you still need load-in parking and you would be paying over cap. A north-side hotel gives you breakfast, free parking, and a better setup for the Monday morning Plano event.
Which refundable holds should I place first tonight?

First hold Plano/Richardson for Sunday and Monday: free breakfast starting around 6, free parking, restaurants nearby, and easy access to Plano. Second hold Waco for Tuesday: late check-in, free parking, breakfast Wednesday morning, and food nearby after the fair. Third hold Round Rock or La Frontera for Wednesday: free parking, breakfast Thursday, and a short drive to the community college meeting. If you only have time for two, do Plano/Richardson and Waco first.
Can you put the final ranking in a short table for the approval email?

Use this: Plan | Rank | Reason. Dallas-in/Austin-out open jaw | 1 | Matches the southbound event order, avoids Thursday Round Rock-to-DFW backtrack, and allows an afternoon one-stop home with a comfortable connection. Dallas round trip | 2 | Potentially cheaper airfare, but adds a long Thursday drive, fuel/tolls, traffic risk, and later return. Driving from Salt Lake | 3 | Helps with materials, but costs too many travel hours and adds fatigue. Hotel holds: Plano/Richardson Sun-Mon, Waco Tue, Round Rock/La Frontera Wed, all refundable if possible with breakfast and parking verified.

messages.content: Open-jaw was approved. Let's move this into reservations. I need Sunday afternoon SLC to Dallas, Thursday afternoon Austin to Salt Lake with one comfortable connection, an SUV for five boxes and the banner, and the three hotels we discussed. They also want a note explaining why we didn't do a Dallas return.

Great. I will keep the flights on one ticket each direction, use DFW inbound unless Love Field is clearly better, and keep hotels refundable where possible. For the return, should I prioritize getting home around dinner over the late nonstop?
Yes. DFW is fine. Flights can be nonrefundable if the schedule is right. Standard SUV preferred. And please request window seats where available.

Best flight set I found: Sun Oct 6, Delta SLC to DFW nonstop, 3:10 pm to 6:45 pm, coach, window requested. Thu Oct 10, American AUS to SLC via Phoenix, 3:05 pm to 7:45 pm, one ticket with a 78-minute Phoenix connection, coach, windows requested on both legs. That return gives you time after the Round Rock meeting without pushing you into a late-night arrival.
Book that, as long as it's not the tight Phoenix connection I saw earlier.

Booked with the 78-minute Phoenix connection, not the short one. I also reserved a pay-later standard SUV: DFW pickup Sunday 7:15 pm, AUS return Thursday 1:30 pm, one-way fee included, unlimited miles, covered cargo area noted. The vehicle class should fit five boxes plus the banner with one rear seat folded if needed.
Hotels next. Free breakfast if you can, no downtown paid parking, and a queen room is fine.

Booked refundable holds: Hampton Inn Dallas/Plano-Richardson, Sun-Mon, two-queen non-smoking, $169 before tax, breakfast from 6, free parking, cancel by Oct 4 at 6 pm, restaurants nearby. Holiday Inn Express Waco South, Tue, queen or two-queen non-smoking, $154, breakfast from 6:30, free parking, 24-hour desk, cancel by Oct 7 at 6 pm. Hampton Inn Austin/Round Rock-La Frontera, Wed, queen non-smoking, $162, breakfast from 6, free parking, restaurants in the same area, cancel by Oct 8 at 6 pm.
On Waco, make sure late check-in is okay if teardown runs long.
Confirmed. Waco has a 24-hour front desk, and I added a late-arrival note. I also noted that you are traveling with recruitment materials and asked for parking that is well lit if available.
Can you reserve the Dallas fair parking too?

Yes. I reserved a refundable garage near the Dallas fair for Monday 3:30 to 9:15 pm, with SUV clearance checked. Keep that receipt with the fair expenses. Plan to leave Plano/Richardson by about 3:15 for load-in.
Perfect. Give me the reimbursement note and final itinerary.

Reimbursement note: Open-jaw air was approved because the event sequence runs south from Plano/Dallas to Fort Worth, Waco, and Round Rock. Returning from Dallas would add a 3-plus-hour Round Rock-to-DFW backtrack after the Thursday meeting, plus fuel, tolls, extra driving time, and return-flight risk. The Austin return uses one comfortable Phoenix connection and arrives Salt Lake around 7:45 pm instead of using the late nonstop. Standard SUV is needed for five boxes and a banner tube; one-way fee is documented. Hotels are under the $185 pre-tax cap and include breakfast and free parking. Final itinerary: Sun Oct 6 Delta SLC-DFW 3:10-6:45, window requested; pick up standard SUV at DFW 7:15 pm; Hampton Plano-Richardson Sun/Mon. Tue Oct 8 Fort Worth visits, evening Waco fair, Holiday Inn Express Waco South. Wed Oct 9 reposition to Round Rock, Hampton Round Rock-La Frontera. Thu Oct 10 Round Rock meeting, return SUV at AUS 1:30 pm, American AUS-PHX-SLC 3:05-7:45, windows requested. Save airfare receipt, Dallas-return comparison, rental receipt, fuel/tolls, hotel folios, Dallas parking, and any materials shipping or baggage receipts.
